principles: Freeze the subject before parallel discovery so every verdict is comparable.
Completeness is demonstrated by coverage plus a clean saturation wave, never by an arbitrary review count.
One module owns epoch state, validity, transitions, signing, status projection and gate decisions.
Efficiency may remove invalidated rework but must not reduce assurance.
drivers: Fail closed across every authoritative mutation and transition boundary.
Reuse existing signed ReviewRun and ReviewPass facts where safe.

options.name: A: Signed frozen inventory epoch with bounded saturation
pros: Directly prevents reviewed material from changing
Aggregates all verified findings before remediation
Supports falsifiable efficiency and quality checks
cons: Adds lifecycle commands and a new gate artifact
Requires integration across several write boundaries

options.name: B: Require N consecutive clean review rounds
cons: N is arbitrary and can miss uncovered lanes
Can mechanically reduce or inflate rounds without proving completeness

options.name: C: Run all reviewers in parallel but allow immediate fixes
cons: Cannot support a trustworthy aggregate inventory

chosen: A: Signed frozen inventory epoch with bounded saturation
rationale: Option A addresses the causal defect: candidate mutation before discovery is complete. It uses bounded waves, required-lane terminal evidence and a completeness critic to prove saturation, while mutation barriers and lineage checks keep every verdict on one cutoff. Options B and C optimize a visible round count without establishing that review was exhaustive or comparable.

preMortem.scenario: A write path bypasses the OPEN barrier
preMortem.trigger: Material hash changes between receipt submissions or finalization
preMortem.consequence: Mixed-cutoff verdicts could create a false saturation receipt
preMortem.mitigation: Revalidate cutoff at every producer and consumer, mark INVALIDATED, and add bypass regression tests for handler, hook, commit and transition boundaries.

preMortem.scenario: Duplicate or forged findings make a wave appear clean
preMortem.trigger: Same identity or unverified duplicate disposition is counted as terminal coverage
preMortem.consequence: A real issue is omitted from the remediation set
preMortem.mitigation: Canonical finding-family disposition, independent verification, signed lane identity and fail-closed duplicate validation.

preMortem.scenario: Wave budget is exhausted while new findings continue
preMortem.trigger: Configured maximum waves reached with nonzero new verified findings
preMortem.consequence: Framework may be tempted to declare PASS for schedule reasons
preMortem.mitigation: Prohibit finalization and require explicit replan, decomposition, root-cause escalation or human adjudication.

preMortem.scenario: Final review reuses the defective cutoff receipt
preMortem.trigger: Remediation creates new material but old receipt remains superficially valid
preMortem.consequence: TEST is entered without reviewing the repaired implementation
preMortem.mitigation: Receipt authorizes only one remediation DEV transition; repair invalidates it for certification and impacted lanes must provide current evidence.

preMortem.trigger: Implementation chooses fewer lanes or hosts to meet speed threshold
preMortem.consequence: Cycle count improves while escaped-defect risk grows
preMortem.mitigation: Make lane/host counts invariant and replay all historical critical/high cases; efficiency is reported separately from gate facts.
